source.title: Input and Weight Space Smoothing for Semi-Supervised Learning

record.tranche_reason: Measures how network size and ABCD training relate to weight perturbation robustness and compares SSL test errors; it does not measure the catalog's training-versus-test gap or the versions' target generalization claims directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-error comparisons for SSL methods and experiments measuring loss changes under adversarial weight perturbations. It does not report natural-label versus random-label generalization, interpolation-width sweeps, architecture comparisons, optimizer test-gap comparisons, or dropout effects. Cited results from other papers are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flat-minima/generalization rationale to develop ABCD and evaluates weight robustness and semi-supervised test error. It does not test any specified version. In particular, its unscaled ascent probes do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or its association with generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that input and weight smoothing are distinct and complementary, and that ABCD combined with VAT achieves performance comparable to the state of the art with modest augmentation and a relatively simple architecture.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies semi-supervised learning and weight-space robustness using ABCD and VAT; the catalog versions concern memorization and train-test generalization, which are not directly tested.
record.method_sensitivity: Network size changes robustness to weight-space perturbations in the half-moon experiment; combining ABCD with VAT changes SSL test error relative to the reported baselines.

fits_no_version.finding: VAT-trained half-moon MLPs have essentially identical decision boundaries and output responses, while wider networks require more ascent steps before training loss visibly increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing width can increase measured weight-space robustness without changing input-space smoothness.

fits_no_version.finding: ABCD-trained weights require more ascent updates before loss divergence than SGD-trained weights; a single interpolation direction also appears flatter around ABCD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ABCD increases local weight-space robustness under the paper's ascent and interpolation probes.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding ABCD to the authors' VAT-plus-entropy implementation reduces test error from 11.81% to 10.11% on CIFAR10 and from 4.10% to 3.63% on SVHN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Combining weight-space and input-space smoothing improves semi-supervised test performance in these settings.

record.peer_reviewed: 2019 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision Workshop (ICCVW)
record.problems: Weight-robustness comparisons are described through plots without numeric ascent-update values. The SSL table reports test error but not training error, so it cannot establish train-test gaps. The half-moon experiment uses a two-dimensional toy dataset.
record.rows_left_out: No table rows omitted. Other Figure 2 right-panel loss-landscape values are figure-only and do not directly report an additional outcome beyond the text's qualitative ABCD-versus-SGD robustness comparison.

untested.parts: Matched natural-label and random-label fitting and held-out performance; random-label fitting is mentioned only through citations.
Held-out error across widths beyond zero training error; the width experiment measures weight robustness instead.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparisons under specified tuning budgets. The discussion of differing VAT implementations confounds optimizer, schedule and preprocessing.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout versus no-dropout held-out error. Describing ABCD as related to dropout does not test dropout.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its ranking of generalization gaps among comparably fitted networks, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of highly memorized examples versus equally sized random removals and subsequent test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: No version-specific verdict is warranted. Figure 2 includes training and test loss along an interpolation path, so the text is not wholly devoid of train/test comparisons; these curves still do not establish V7's specified relationship. The record's statement that no table rows were omitted is inaccurate, but the omitted method-performance rows do not bear on V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Natural-label versus random-label training and held-out accuracy.
Test error across widths beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error.
Removing memorized examples and its effect on test accuracy.
